title: N. C. Davis and the Phillips Chapel juvenile band
summary: Nathaniel C. Davis, from a musical family, taught the children's band at Phillips Chapel; they played marches and hymns and Cheatham was faking the reading.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And, now, this N. C. Davis --
That was a teacher that was brought into the little chapel where we were gathered to have a juvenile band. He was a teacher, dean of the Phillips Chapel brought this teacher in to instruct us kids --
Well his name -- what is the N. C. stand for?

Nathaniel C. Davis, yes. He was a very famous man and he had a brother, C. M. Davis, trumpet player and he had a brother, O. B. Davis, who died in New York, he was a great drummer. And he had a sister which was a fine -- they're all a family of musicians.
Now when you were playing in this school band, what sort of music were you playing there?
Well, the first tune that we played was called, 'Action Quick Step.' It was a little march, like. See this was in the Phillips Chapel, where just the dean de-

cided to have this group, I mean the kids played and he brought in, naturally, little church songs and marches and things for us supposed to play. I guess I was about the only one who wasn't reading, but I was faking, they didn't know the difference.
We played little marches and things like that. For quite a long time, and church hymns.
Was there anyone else in that band that we would've heard of?
Because they're all -- all of them dropped out of music, you know, except myself -- and the drummer the drummer -- no, I was the only one that continued out of the whole group.
